What they said: Punchbowl reports COLT has been quietly pushing negotiators for targeted technical fixes to the NHPA section (Sec. 2301) and circulating a discussion paper with proposed amendments. Its executive director expects the bill to pass the Senate, so the group is working on the text rather than against the bill. The amendments themselves were not visible.

Group: NATHPO and Standing Rock Sioux Tribe
What they said: NATHPO opposes the bill as written and argues the NHPA provisions "cannot be fixed through amendment," the opposite of COLT's approach. Standing Rock's statement (Chairman Sitting Bear, Oct. 30, posted Nov. 3) says the bill would weaken laws protecting treaty rights, trust resources and cultural resources.

Group: NRECA and APPA (electric co-ops and public power)
What they said: Joint letter "strongly support[s]" the bill but makes continued support contingent on a "technical change" in the manager's amendment that avoids new, burdensome FERC regulation of cooperatives and public power. The letter cites no section. Notable because these groups opposed the 2024 deal over federal transmission siting.

Group: Teamsters, Iron Workers, Boilermakers, SMART and other unions
What they said: Letter shared with Politico urges the four lead negotiators to "swiftly pass" S. 5653, framed around clean energy built by union members. The visible signer list is cut off, so the full roster is not confirmed.
The transit trade group endorsed S. 5653 as legislation that "modernizes Federal environmental review and permitting."
President Tracy Stone-Manning (BLM director under Biden) says the bill puts public lands on "a one-way path to industrial development" and that elected officials "should reject it."
